paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהַי֙ אַתָּ֔ה אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ פֶּ֑לֶא עֵצ֥וֹת מֵֽרָח֖וֹק אֱמ֥וּנָה אֹֽמֶן׃

i18n.en: YHWH, you are my God; I will exalt you, I will praise your name, for you have done a wonder — plans formed long ago, in faithfulness and truth.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהַי֙ אַתָּ֔ה אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ פֶּ֑לֶא עֵצ֥וֹת מֵֽרָח֖וֹק אֱמ֥וּנָה אֹֽמֶן׃

notes.official:
The chapter turns from the judgment-oracle of chapter 24 to a first-person thanksgiving hymn. *YHWH ʾĕlōhay ʾattāh* 'YHWH, you are my God' opens the praise; the suffixed *ʾĕlōhay* ('my God', 1cs) is rendered plainly, and the corpus 'the Elohim' convention is deliberately **not** applied to a vocative doxology, exactly as at Isa 53:4 (*mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm* 'struck down by God') and 24:15 (*ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'the God of Israel'): the entry that renders 'the Elohim' is scoped to the Genesis-1 narrative frame and cannot govern a first-person cry of praise (Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1-39*, AB 19, 2000).

*ʿāśîṯā peleʾ* 'you have done a wonder' (*peleʾ*, the extraordinary deed) is glossed 'wonder'; *ʿēṣôṯ mē-rāḥôq* is rendered 'plans formed long ago' — *ʿēṣāh* 'counsel, plan' with *mē-rāḥôq* read temporally ('from of old', JPS 'counsels of old'), a purpose settled in advance and now carried out (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13-27*, Continental, 1997). The closing *ʾĕmûnāh ʾōmen* piles two nouns from the same root *ʾmn* 'be firm, reliable'; ASV/JPS render 'faithfulness and truth', which the translation keeps, noting that the pair is an intensified single notion ('sure, steadfast faithfulness', a hendiadys) rather than two distinct attributes.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י שַׂ֤מְתָּ מֵעִיר֙ לַגָּ֔ל קִרְיָ֥ה בְצוּרָ֖ה לְמַפֵּלָ֑ה אַרְמ֤וֹן זָרִים֙ מֵעִ֔יר לְעוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִבָּנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: For you have made of a city a heap of stones, of a fortified town a ruin; the citadel of strangers is a city no more, it will never be rebuilt.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י שַׂ֤מְתָּ מֵעִיר֙ לַגָּ֔ל קִרְיָ֥ה בְצוּרָ֖ה לְמַפֵּלָ֑ה אַרְמ֤וֹן זָרִים֙ מֵעִ֔יר לְעוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִבָּנֶֽה׃

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֖ן יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ עַם־עָ֑ז קִרְיַ֛ת גּוֹיִ֥ם עָרִיצִ֖ים יִירָאֽוּךָ׃

i18n.en: Therefore a strong people will honor you, the town of ruthless nations will fear you.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֖ן יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ עַם־עָ֑ז קִרְיַ֛ת גּוֹיִ֥ם עָרִיצִ֖ים יִירָאֽוּךָ׃

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הָיִ֨יתָ מָע֥וֹז לַדָּ֛ל מָע֥וֹז לָאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּצַּר־ל֑וֹ מַחְסֶ֤ה מִזֶּ֙רֶם֙ צֵ֣ל מֵחֹ֔רֶב כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ עָרִיצִ֖ים כְּזֶ֥רֶם קִֽיר׃

i18n.en: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat; for the blast of the ruthless was like a rainstorm against a wall.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־הָיִ֨יתָ מָע֥וֹז לַדָּ֛ל מָע֥וֹז לָאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּצַּר־ל֑וֹ מַחְסֶ֤ה מִזֶּ֙רֶם֙ צֵ֣ל מֵחֹ֔רֶב כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ עָרִיצִ֖ים כְּזֶ֥רֶם קִֽיר׃

paragraphs.text: כְּחֹ֣רֶב בְּצָי֔וֹן שְׁא֥וֹן זָרִ֖ים תַּכְנִ֑יעַ חֹ֚רֶב בְּצֵ֣ל עָ֔ב זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Like heat in a parched land you subdue the uproar of strangers; as heat is subdued by the shadow of a cloud, so the song of the ruthless is brought low.
i18n.he: כְּחֹ֣רֶב בְּצָי֔וֹן שְׁא֥וֹן זָרִ֖ים תַּכְנִ֑יעַ חֹ֚רֶב בְּצֵ֣ל עָ֔ב זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה׃ (פ)

notes.official: *zᵉmîr ʿārîṣîm yaʿăneh* is a double crux. *zᵉmîr* may be 'song' (√*zmr* I, so ASV/JPS 'the song of the terrible ones') or 'pruning / a lopped branch' (√*zmr* II, a vine-shoot cut down); *yaʿăneh* may be 'is brought low / humbled' (√*ʿnh* II) or 'is answered / responds' (√*ʿnh* I). The translation follows the majority 'the song of the ruthless is brought low' (ASV/JPS) — the tyrants' exultant song subdued as the heat is subdued by a cloud's shadow in the same verse's simile — with the botanical and 'answered/silenced' readings recorded as alternatives (Wildberger; Kaiser, *Isaiah 13-39*, OTL, 1974). *zārîm* 'strangers, foreigners' (also 25:2) is rendered 'strangers'.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת לְכָל־הָֽעַמִּים֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה מִשְׁתֵּ֥ה שְׁמָנִ֖ים מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה שְׁמָרִ֑ים שְׁמָנִים֙ מְמֻ֣חָיִ֔ם שְׁמָרִ֖ים מְזֻקָּקִֽים׃

i18n.en: And on this mountain YHWH of hosts will make for all the peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees — of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.
i18n.he: וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת לְכָל־הָֽעַמִּים֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה מִשְׁתֵּ֥ה שְׁמָנִ֖ים מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה שְׁמָרִ֑ים שְׁמָנִים֙ מְמֻ֣חָיִ֔ם שְׁמָרִ֖ים מְזֻקָּקִֽים׃

notes.official:
The hymn opens onto the chapter's canon-salient image: *wᵉʿāśāh YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ lᵉ-ḵol-hā-ʿammîm bā-hār ha-zzeh mišteh* — 'YHWH of hosts will make for all the peoples on this mountain a feast'. The divine title *YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is rendered 'YHWH of hosts' (the overlay entry, its *appliesTo* extended from Isa 6 to 25:6); the heavenly-host / divine-assembly reading of *ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is confined to that entry's apparatus and not surfaced in the line.

*mišteh šᵉmānîm mišteh šᵉmārîm* 'a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees' names a lavish banquet — *šᵉmānîm* rich, fatty foods; *šᵉmārîm* wine matured on its lees; *mᵉmuḥāyim* 'full of marrow' and *mᵉzuqqāqîm* 'well refined'. The point is the inclusive scope: the feast is spread 'for all the peoples' (*lᵉ-ḵol-hā-ʿammîm*) on 'this mountain', that is, Zion — an eschatological banquet for the nations (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp). The messianic-banquet reception this image feeds — the eschatological feast with Abraham of Matt 8:11, the great-banquet parable of Luke 14:15-24, the marriage-supper of Rev 19:9 — is left to the apparatus as a hedged comparative datum and not committed in the text.

paragraphs.text: וּבִלַּע֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה פְּנֵֽי־הַלּ֥וֹט ׀ הַלּ֖וֹט עַל־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה הַנְּסוּכָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: And on this mountain he will swallow up the face of the shroud that shrouds all the peoples, and the veil that is spread over all the nations.
i18n.he: וּבִלַּע֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה פְּנֵֽי־הַלּ֥וֹט ׀ הַלּ֖וֹט עַל־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה הַנְּסוּכָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

notes.official: *û-ḇillaʿ bā-hār ha-zzeh pᵉnê-hal-lôṭ hal-lôṭ ʿal-kol-hā-ʿammîm* — on the same mountain YHWH 'will swallow up (*billaʿ*, √*blʿ*) the face of the shroud that shrouds all the peoples'. The verb *billaʿ* 'swallow up' here means destroy / do away with, and it is the very verb that opens 25:8 (of death) — a deliberate catchword binding the banquet to the abolition of death. The doubled *hal-lôṭ hal-lôṭ* (with *paseq*) is from *lwṭ* 'to wrap, envelop'; it may be a funerary shroud, a mourning-veil, or a blinding covering. The parallel *ha-massēḵāh han-nᵉsûḵāh* 'the veil that is spread / woven over all the nations' confirms the covering-image. The translation keeps the standard 'shroud … veil' (ASV/JPS), with the funerary reading — the covering as a death-shroud over the nations, tying 25:7 to the death-swallowing of 25:8 — noted as the reading the context favours (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp).

paragraphs.text: בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֙וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וּמָחָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה דִּמְעָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־פָּנִ֑ים וְחֶרְפַּ֣ת עַמּ֗וֹ יָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: He has swallowed up death forever; and the Lord YHWH will wipe away the tears from all faces, and the reproach of his people he will remove from off all the earth; for YHWH has spoken.
i18n.he: בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֙וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וּמָחָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה דִּמְעָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־פָּנִ֑ים וְחֶרְפַּ֣ת עַמּ֗וֹ יָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ (פ)

notes.official:
*billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ* 'he has swallowed up death forever' is the chapter's load-bearing line and a major cross-corpus site. The verb is again *billaʿ* 'swallow up' (from 25:7); its subject is YHWH, and *ham-māweṯ* 'death' is its object. The translation renders *māweṯ* as the abstract 'death' (lower-case), **not** a personified 'Death': the Northwest-Semitic death-god substrate is real but is kept in the apparatus, not imposed on the line (ASV 'He hath swallowed up death for ever'; JPS same).

**The Ugaritic Môtu reversal (hedged).** Hebrew *māweṯ* shares the proto-Semitic root √*mwt* with Ugaritic *mt* (vocalized *Môtu*), the Death-god of the Baal Cycle whose standing iconography is a vast throat that swallows gods — in KTU 1.5 *Môtu* 'the Swallower' swallows Baʿlu himself. Here the verb *blʿ* 'swallow' is turned against Death: the Swallower is himself swallowed. The reversal of the Ugaritic image is widely noted (J. Day, *God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea*, 1985; the central *mot-mavet-death-personified* entry, whose *appliesTo* is extended to this verse). This is a comparative-history resonance, stated as such and not resolved into the line.

**Reception and the *lā-neṣaḥ* variant (hedged).** *lā-neṣaḥ* is rendered 'forever' (the standard MT sense 'in perpetuity'). The Old Greek instead inverts the clause — *katépien ho thánatos ischýsas* 'Death, having prevailed, swallowed up' (Death as subject) — while 1 Cor 15:54 cites the verse in the MT's direction but reads *neṣaḥ* as 'victory': *katepóthē ho thánatos eis nîkos* 'Death is swallowed up in victory' (the later-Hebrew/Aramaic sense of *nṣḥ*). The next clause, *û-māḥāh … dimʿāh mē-ʿal kol-pānîm* 'he will wipe away tears from all faces', is echoed at Rev 21:4 ('he will wipe away every tear … death shall be no more'). These are versional and reception data, disclosed for audit and not read back into the MT line (Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1-39*, AB 19, 2000).

**Divine name.** *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* is the compound name (*ʾăḏōnāy* + the Tetragrammaton pointed with *ʾĕlōhîm*-vowels), rendered 'the Lord YHWH' — the corpus compound-name convention ('Lord YHWH', per the Ezekiel/Genesis *adonai-yhwh* entries), kept distinct from the standalone *ʾăḏōnāy* 'the Lord' of Isa 6.

paragraphs.text: וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא הִנֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֥ינוּ זֶ֛ה קִוִּ֥ינוּ ל֖וֹ וְיֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נוּ זֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קִוִּ֣ינוּ ל֔וֹ נָגִ֥ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֖ה בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And in that day it will be said: ‘Behold, this is our God; we waited for him, that he might save us. This is YHWH; we waited for him. Let us be glad and rejoice in his salvation.’
i18n.he: וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא הִנֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֥ינוּ זֶ֛ה קִוִּ֥ינוּ ל֖וֹ וְיֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נוּ זֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קִוִּ֣ינוּ ל֔וֹ נָגִ֥ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֖ה בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

notes.official: The answering acclamation *hinnēh ʾĕlōhênû zeh* 'Behold, this is our God' renders the suffixed *ʾĕlōhênû* ('our God', 1cp) plainly; as at 25:1, the 'the Elohim' convention is deliberately not applied to a confessional cry of recognition and joy (the Isa 53:4 / 24:15 precedent). *qiwwînû lô* 'we waited for him' (√*qwh* 'wait, hope') and *bî-šûʿāṯô* 'in his salvation' (√*yšʿ*) are rendered at the standard surface (ASV/JPS).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־תָנ֥וּחַ יַד־יְהוָ֖ה בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְנָ֤דוֹשׁ מוֹאָב֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כְּהִדּ֥וּשׁ מַתְבֵּ֖ן במי [בְּמ֥וֹ] מַדְמֵנָֽה׃

i18n.en: For the hand of YHWH will rest on this mountain, and Moab will be trodden down in its place, as straw is trodden down in a dung-pit.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־תָנ֥וּחַ יַד־יְהוָ֖ה בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְנָ֤דוֹשׁ מוֹאָב֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כְּהִדּ֥וּשׁ מַתְבֵּ֖ן במי [בְּמ֥וֹ] מַדְמֵנָֽה׃

notes.official: The oracle turns to judgment on Moab. *wᵉnāḏôš môʾāḇ taḥtāyw* 'Moab will be trodden down in its place' pictures Moab threshed like straw. The closing phrase carries a *ketiv/qere*: the consonantal text (*ketiv*) reads *bᵉmê* בְּמֵי 'in the water(s) of', the Masoretic reading-tradition (*qere*) reads *bᵉmô* בְּמוֹ 'in / within'; per the qere-first rule the line translates the qere, 'in a dung-pit' (*madmēnāh*, √*dmn* 'dung'; JPS 'dunghill'), with the ketiv 'in the water of a dunghill' (straw trodden into liquid manure, so ASV) recorded. *madmēnāh* may also pun on the Moabite place-name *Madmēn* (Jer 48:2). *yaḏ-YHWH* 'the hand of YHWH' is rendered plainly (the central *yad-yhwh* entry is Ezekiel-scoped and not applied).

paragraphs.text: וּפֵרַ֤שׂ יָדָיו֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְפָרֵ֥שׂ הַשֹּׂחֶ֖ה לִשְׂח֑וֹת וְהִשְׁפִּיל֙ גַּֽאֲוָת֔וֹ עִ֖ם אָרְבּ֥וֹת יָדָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim; but he will bring down his pride together with the cunning of his hands.
i18n.he: וּפֵרַ֤שׂ יָדָיו֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְפָרֵ֥שׂ הַשֹּׂחֶ֖ה לִשְׂח֑וֹת וְהִשְׁפִּיל֙ גַּֽאֲוָת֔וֹ עִ֖ם אָרְבּ֥וֹת יָדָֽיו׃

notes.official: Moab 'spreads out his hands (*û-p̄ēraś yāḏāyw*) within it, as a swimmer (*haś-śōḥeh*) spreads to swim'. The subject of *wᵉhišpîl* 'he will bring down' is YHWH, carried over from 25:10, read actively; JPS reads the passive 'his pride shall be brought down'. *ʾārᵉbôṯ yāḏāyw* is a crux: ASV/JPS 'the cunning of his hands' (√*ʾrb* 'lie in wait, be crafty'), against 'the strokes / spreadings of his hands' (the swimmer's motions); the translation follows 'the cunning of his hands' (Wildberger; Kaiser).

paragraphs.text: וּמִבְצַ֞ר מִשְׂגַּ֣ב חוֹמֹתֶ֗יךָ הֵשַׁ֥ח הִשְׁפִּ֛יל הִגִּ֥יעַ לָאָ֖רֶץ עַד־עָפָֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the high fortress of your walls he has brought down, laid low, brought to the ground, to the dust.
i18n.he: וּמִבְצַ֞ר מִשְׂגַּ֣ב חוֹמֹתֶ֗יךָ הֵשַׁ֥ח הִשְׁפִּ֛יל הִגִּ֥יעַ לָאָ֖רֶץ עַד־עָפָֽר׃ (ס)

notes.official: The demolition closes with an apostrophe to Moab's stronghold: *ûmiḇṣar miśgaḇ ḥômōṯeḵā* 'the high fortress of your walls' — the 2ms 'your' addressed directly to Moab — brought down by three piled verbs: *hēšaḥ* 'bowed down' (√*šwḥ*/*šḥḥ*), *hišpîl* 'laid low', *higgîaʿ lā-ʾāreṣ* 'brought to the ground', ending *ʿaḏ-ʿāp̄ār* 'to the dust'. Standard rendering (ASV/JPS); no lens.
